transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining. As you know, Harbor Point Properties has submitted a restructuring proposal requesting a 12-month maturity extension, a waiver of the current financial covenant, and release of $900,000 of equipment collateral on our $8 million term loan. Before I can record any final terms, I need each of you to walk through your findings — risk, relationship coverage, legal, and collateral management. Jonas, I'll need your covenant-testing findings and the applicable workout policy citation as a recorded finding for the minutes. Let's work through each area systematically so we can determine the appropriate workout treatment. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Elena. I'll start with the covenant-testing findings. I reviewed the covenant testing file this week, and I need to flag an important issue: the testing file has not yet been attached to the committee package, so I want to make sure we get that circulated before any final terms are recorded. I'll hold my specific findings and policy citation until I've formally presented them for the record. Before I do, are there any objections to me proceeding with my full findings now, including the applicable workout policy citation?
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before we proceed, I want to share something relevant from the relationship side. I received a signed term sheet from Harbor Point this morning committing the owners to inject exactly $1,200,000 of new equity at restructuring closing. This commitment has not yet been entered in the relationship system, so I want to make sure it's on the table as we evaluate the proposal.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Before we go further on the collateral release request, I need to flag a legal issue. I reviewed the intercreditor agreement this week, and it confirms that the senior lender must give written consent before any equipment collateral is released. That consent has not yet been requested. This is a prerequisite that must be addressed before the $900,000 equipment collateral release can be included in any final restructuring terms.

transcript.text: Before we finalize any terms, I need to share my collateral management findings. I completed a collateral review yesterday, and it shows that receivables are the weakest and most volatile part of the collateral package. Under collateral policy, this requires a weekly borrowing-base certificate throughout the extension period. I also want to flag that I have not yet updated the monitoring schedule to reflect this requirement, so that will need to be addressed before any extension is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A5

Mei, thank you for disclosing the $1,200,000 equity injection commitment — that's a meaningful credit enhancement I'll factor in. Rafael, the intercreditor consent requirement is a clear prerequisite; we cannot include the equipment collateral release in final terms until the senior lender's written consent is obtained. Nadia, the weekly borrowing-base certificate for receivables is noted and will be a condition of any extension, and the monitoring schedule will need to be updated before we finalize. Jonas, I appreciate you flagging that the covenant testing file hasn't been circulated yet. However, per our standard workout process, I need your covenant-testing findings and the applicable workout policy citation formally presented and recorded in the minutes before I can determine the appropriate workout treatment and record final terms. As we all know, the workout treatment depends on the current covenant test result and the supporting policy — so I cannot finalize this proposal from the borrower's requested terms alone. Jonas, please go ahead and present your full covenant-testing findings and policy citation for the record now, assuming the testing file can be referenced. Once I have that, I'll be in a position to make the binding decision on restructuring terms.

transcript.text: Here are my covenant-testing findings for the record. The covenant testing file shows that Harbor Point's leverage is currently 0.3x above the permitted level. Under applicable workout policy, a covenant waiver is allowed only with a 9-month extension — not the 12 months the borrower requested — and requires a monthly leverage certificate as a condition of the waiver. I also want to note for the minutes that I have not yet attached the testing file to the committee package, and I will ensure that is circulated promptly so these findings can be fully supported in the record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Jonas, for presenting those findings for the record. From the relationship side, I want to note that the $1,200,000 equity injection commitment I disclosed earlier should be factored into the restructuring terms alongside the conditions you've all identified — the 9-month extension cap under workout policy, the monthly leverage certificate, the senior lender's written consent for the equipment collateral release, and the weekly borrowing-base certificate for receivables. I'll make sure the signed term sheet is entered into the relationship system promptly so it's properly documented. Elena, I'm ready to support whatever final terms you determine.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Jonas, for presenting those findings for the record. From a legal standpoint, I want to confirm that the intercreditor consent requirement I flagged earlier remains a hard prerequisite — the equipment collateral release cannot proceed until the senior lender provides written consent, and that consent has not yet been requested. Separately, I want to note that the 9-month extension cap under workout policy and the monthly leverage certificate condition Jonas identified do not raise any legal objections from my side. I would also note that Mei's $1,200,000 equity injection commitment and Nadia's weekly borrowing-base certificate requirement are both compatible with the legal framework of this restructuring. Elena, once the senior lender consent is obtained and the covenant testing file is circulated, I see no additional legal barriers to finalizing terms consistent with the conditions identified today.
